newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish president delays picking new prime minister.
newsitem.headline: Turkish president delays picking new prime minister.

text.p: Turkish President Suleyman Demirel on Friday delayed a decision on choosing a candidate to be prime minister, a holdup that hurt conservative Tansu Ciller's chances of heading a new coalition with the Islamists.
Demirel's office said his schedule for the day did not include any talks aimed at filling a power vacuum left by the resignation of Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan this week.

Ciller, the pro-Western foreign minister who previously served as Turkey's first woman prime minister, has been among the favourites to replace Erbakan. Opposition head Mesut Yilmaz is another leading contender.
Commentators said the president did not favour Ciller, Islamist Erbakan's ally in an "odd couple" coalition for the last year.
"The president does not want to give priority to Ciller," the Hurriyet daily quoted a source close to Demirel as saying.
"If he had wanted to do that he would not have wasted Turkey's time. He would have asked her to form a new government as soon as Erbakan resigned," the unnamed source said.
Erbakan, NATO member Turkey's first Islamist leader, resigned on Wednesday after months of pressure from the secularist military.
He asked Demirel to approve a plan to put Ciller at the head of a new coalition with the Islamists that would take Turkey to early elections by next spring at the latest.
Demirel gave no clues after talks with opposition leaders on Thursday about how he would deal with the crisis.
Motherland Party leader Yilmaz, a former prime minister, could have trouble finding the parliamentary majority needed to approve any government he set up.
